projectDescription: A curated library for the tools and documentation I come across while learning and building. Anyone can browse and filter the public gallery, while a private admin panel lets me add, edit and categorise everything myself.
projectWhy: I kept losing useful tools in bookmarks and open tabs, and wanted one place I'd actually use every day
I skipped all-in-one platforms like Supabase on purpose, to learn the backend fundamentals they usually handle for you
I wanted to practise a realistic full-stack workflow, from database design to deployment
projectLearned: Designing a PostgreSQL schema with Prisma, including many-to-many relations and migrations
Building session-based auth with express-session and bcrypt, gated by middleware on write routes
Deploying across Vercel, Render and Neon, with an API rewrite that keeps the session cookie first-party

projectDescription: An interactive sticker board that doubles as my portfolio. Every sticker represents something about me, and some of them open pages, switch the theme or toggle sound. A fuzzy search bar and a legend make sure the playfulness never gets in the way of finding things.
projectWhy: My first portfolio kept getting the same feedback: be more creative, but keep it usable
I wanted something that shows who I am, not just what I can code
A generic template felt like it would lead to a generic company
projectLearned: Making a pixel-based, draggable layout fit any screen by scaling it as one unit
Building a fuzzy search with Fuse.js over content stored in JSON
Sending contact form emails server-side with the Resend API
Keeping all content data-driven, so updating the site means editing JSON, not components
